sm: A University of Tennessee Institute of Agriculture study finds a traditional Tennessee Thanksgiving dinner for ten costs about $121.15, down about 6 percent from $128.50 last year. Turkey prices are up about 13 percent, nearly two dollars a pound, averaging $30.85 per turkey, while ham averages $18.39 and is cheaper than last year. Researchers suggest potluck-style meals to save, and note that local food pantries can help.
